text: He asks you to pray for his eyes.
Nothing happens to his eyes. You pray again the next day, and the next week. They stay dark.
You write it down honestly. Not every prayer is answered the way you ask it.
A blind man begs at the same Temple gate where the lame man used to sit. He has heard what happened there, and he asks the believers to pray for him.
To see. And if not that, to stop being invisible.
speaker: Tobiah

text: He turns his face toward your voice.
I still can’t see. But I eat with forty people every night, and they all know my name. I was invisible, scribe. Now I’m not.
speaker: Tobiah

text: I still can’t see. But I eat with forty people every night, and they all know my name. I was invisible, daughter. Now I’m not.
speaker: Tobiah

text: He runs his fingers along the fringes and laughs. “A Pharisee’s cloak, on a quarryman.”
He runs his fingers along the fringes and laughs. “A scribe’s cloak, on a quarryman.”
You put your hands over his eyes and pray, as Peter prayed at the gate, in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth.
Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
